cards.example: Climate change is one of the biggest challenges that our generation will have to deal with.
Scientists warn that global warming could raise sea levels and flood many coastal cities.
Cars, factories and farms release greenhouse gas emissions that trap heat in the atmosphere.
Taking the train instead of flying is an easy way to reduce your carbon footprint.
Hungary should invest more in renewable energy, especially solar power, as we have plenty of sunshine.
Burning fossil fuels such as coal and oil releases huge amounts of carbon dioxide into the air.
Air pollution in big cities can cause serious breathing problems, especially for young children.
In our block of flats, everybody is expected to sort waste into paper, plastic and glass.
Many cafés have stopped selling single-use plastic straws and cups in order to protect the oceans.
Most of our rubbish ends up in a landfill, where some of it takes centuries to decompose.
Biodegradable packaging breaks down naturally and causes much less harm to the environment.
The Hungarian meadow viper is an endangered species that survives only in a few protected areas.
Many animals are facing extinction because people are destroying the forests where they live.
Building new motorways destroys the natural habitat of many birds and small animals.
Deforestation in the Amazon rainforest speeds up climate change and threatens thousands of species.
Last summer's drought was so severe that farmers on the Great Plain lost most of their crops.
Extreme weather events such as storms and floods are becoming more frequent all over Europe.
During the heatwave, elderly people were advised to stay indoors and drink plenty of water.
Cycling to school is a cheap, healthy and environmentally friendly way to get around town.
We need a more sustainable lifestyle that does not use up the planet's limited resources.
If we keep wasting natural resources, future generations may not have enough clean drinking water.
Families can cut down on energy use by switching off lights and unplugging unused devices.
It is important to dispose of old batteries properly because they contain toxic chemicals.
Toxic waste from a nearby factory got into the river and killed thousands of fish.
My parents installed solar panels on our roof, and now our electricity bills are much lower.
Replacing old light bulbs with energy-efficient LED lamps saves both money and electricity.
Urban areas are often noisy and crowded, but they offer better jobs and public services.
Many young people leave rural areas because there are few jobs and little to do there.
More and more families move to the suburbs to have a garden and a quieter life.
Buses and trams in Budapest get terribly overcrowded during the morning rush hour.
Cities need more green spaces where residents can relax and children can play safely.
People who litter in parks should be fined, because they spoil the environment for everyone.
Young people today are more environmentally conscious than their grandparents were at their age.
Our daily choices, such as what we eat and buy, have an impact on the environment.
Rising sea levels pose a threat to millions of people living in coastal areas.
Governments must take action now instead of just promising to cut emissions in the future.
Scientists say that some of the damage caused by global warming is already irreversible.
The new national park will protect local wildlife, including rare birds and wild cats.

cards.meaning: itt az ideje, hogy; legfőbb ideje, hogy
cards.example: It is high time we stopped using so much plastic and started taking recycling seriously.
Investing in public transport will benefit both the environment and the economy in the long run.
